h: The Hidden Light and the Protection of Shabbat
The primordial light, the Tree of Knowledge, and the guarding of Shabbat reveal the struggle to separate good from evil.
Primordial Light and the Second Shabbat Meal

p: אוֹמְרִים בִּסְעוּדַת שַׁחֲרִית: "נְהוֹרֵיהּ יִשְׁרֵי בָהּ",
— We recite at the morning meal of Shabbat: "May His light dwell within it,"
הַיְינוּ אוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן,
— meaning the Primordial Light,
דְּאִיתָא בְּסֵפֶר הַבָּהִיר:
— as brought in Sefer HaBahir:
"וְנִבְרָא אוֹר גָּדוֹל וְכוּלֵי,
— "And a great light was created, etc.,
וְצָפָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁאֵין יְכוֹלִין לְסָבְלָם,
— and the Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw that they could not endure it;
לָקַח שְׁבִיעִי וְשָׂם לָהּ בִּמְקוֹמוֹ,
— He took the seventh part and set it in its place,
וְהַשְּׁאָר גְּנָזוֹ לַצַּדִּיקִים לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא וְכוּלֵי";
— and the remainder He concealed for the righteous in the World to Come, etc.";
וְזֶהוּ "נְהוֹרֵיהּ יִשְׁרֵי בָהּ",
— and this is "May His light dwell within it,"
שֶׁבְּשַׁבָּת יְכוֹלִין לִזְכּוֹת לָאוֹר שֶׁגָּנוּז לֶעָתִיד לָבוֹא.
— signifying that on Shabbat we can merit the light concealed for the World to Come.
דְּשַׁבָּת מֵעֵין עוֹלָם הַבָּא,
— For Shabbat is a foretaste of the World to Come,
אֶחָד מִשִּׁשִּׁים לְעוֹלָם הַבָּא (בְּרָכוֹת נז:).
— one-sixtieth of the World to Come (Berakhot 57b).
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ מו עַמּוּד א):
— And in the holy Zohar (in this portion, 46a):
"וְכִי טוֹב הוּא לְאַגְנָזָא לֵיהּ דְּלָא יֵהֲנוּן מִנֵּיהּ חַיָּיבֵי עָלְמָא",
— "'And that it was good'—to conceal it so that the wicked of the world would not benefit from it,"
וְכֵן נִרְאֶה מֵהַמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה יא)
— and so it appears from the Midrash (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 11)
דְּדָרַשׁ לָהּ מִפָּסוּק "וַיִּמָּנַע מֵרְשָׁעִים אוֹרָם".
— which expounded it from the verse: "And from the wicked their light is withheld."
וְיֵשׁ לְהָבִין,
— And we must understand:
הָא גַּם בְּשַׁבָּת אֵין כָּל אֶחָד מִיִּשְׂרָאֵל זוֹכֶה לְהַרְגִּישׁ מֵאוֹר הַגָּנוּז,
— behold, even on Shabbat not every individual of Israel merits to feel the concealed light,
רַק מִי שֶׁרָאוּי לִזְכּוֹת;
— only one who is worthy to merit;
וְלָמָּה נִגְנַז, וְיִהְיֶה וְלֹא יִזְכּוּ הָרְשָׁעִים לֵהָנוֹת מֵאוֹרוֹ?
— so why was it hidden—let it remain manifest, and the wicked simply will not merit to enjoy its light?
גַּם עִיקַּר הָאוֹר אִיתָא (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה ג):
— Furthermore, regarding the essence of the light it is stated (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 3):
שֶׁנִּתְעַטֵּף בָּהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא כְּשַׂלְמָה
— that the Holy One, blessed be He, wrapped Himself in it like a garment
וְהִבְהִיק זִיו הֲדָרוֹ מִסּוֹף הָעוֹלָם וְעַד סוֹפוֹ וְכוּלֵי,
— and the splendor of His majesty radiated from one end of the world to the other, etc.;
וְאִם כֵּן אִם יֵהֲנוּ הָרְשָׁעִים מִמֶּנּוּ וְיִזְכּוּ לְאוֹרוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא,
— and if so, if the wicked were to benefit from it and merit the light of the Holy One, blessed be He,
שׁוּב לֹא יִהְיוּ רְשָׁעִים;
— they would no longer be wicked;
וּכְשֶׁיִּהְיוּ רְשָׁעִים בְּוַדַּאי לֹא יֵהֲנוּ מִמֶּנּוּ,
— and while they remain wicked they surely would not benefit from it,
וּמִמַּה נַפְשָׁךְ לָמָּה נִגְנַז?
— so whichever way you look at it, why was it concealed?
אַף בֶּאֱמֶת קָשֶׁה כְּעֵין קוּשְׁיָא זוֹ
— Indeed, in truth, an analogous difficulty arises
בְּמַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְעַתָּה פֶּן יִשְׁלַח יָדוֹ וְלָקַח גַּם מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים וְאָכַל וָחַי לְעֹלָם",
— concerning that which is said: "And now, lest he put forth his hand and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever";
וְקָשֶׁה, אִם הָיָה אֲכִילַת עֵץ הַחַיִּים גּוֹרֵם דֶּרֶךְ סְגֻלָּה לִהְיוֹת חַי לְעוֹלָם,
— and it is difficult: if eating of the tree of life operated as a metaphysical catalyst to live forever,
בְּוַדַּאי הָיָה בְּיַד הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְשַׁנּוֹת טִבְעוֹ: יֹאכַל וְלֹא יִחְיֶה.
— surely it was in the power of the Holy One, blessed be He, to alter its nature: that he eat and not live!
וּבְתַנָּא דְבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ אִיתָא: "וְאֵין עֵץ חַיִּים אֶלָּא תוֹרָה",
— And in Tanna DeBei Eliyahu it is taught: "And the tree of life is nothing other than Torah";
וּבַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ב, ס עַמּוּד ב): "וְאֵין עֵץ אֶלָּא תוֹרָה, וְאֵין עֵץ אֶלָּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא",
— and in the holy Zohar (Part II, 60b): "And 'tree' is Torah, and 'tree' is the Holy One, blessed be He";
וְאִם כֵּן תִּקְשֶׁה נַמֵּי: יֹאכַל וְיִחְיֶה לְעוֹלָם!
— and if so, the difficulty remains: let him eat and live forever!
אַךְ הָעִנְיָן,
— However, the matter is,
שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שֶׁאָכַל מֵעֵץ הַדַּעַת נַעֲשָׂה הָעִרְבּוּב טוֹב וָרָע,
— that because he ate from the tree of knowledge, an intermingling of good and evil was created,
וְאִם הָיָה אוֹכֵל גַּם מֵעֵץ הַחַיִּים אַחַר כָּךְ,
— and had he eaten also from the tree of life afterward,
הָיָה הַטּוֹב שֶׁבּוֹ זוֹכֶה שֶׁיֹּאכַל וְיִחְיֶה לְעוֹלָם
— the good within him would have merited that he eat and live forever,
וְהָרַע שֶׁבּוֹ הָיָה מִתְגַּבֵּר בְּכָל פַּעַם.
— while the evil within him would have intensified constantly.
וּבֶאֱמֶת נִצְרָךְ הַמִּיתָה לְהָרַע
— And in truth death was necessary for the evil,
לְהַפְרִיד הָרַע מִן הַטּוֹב
— in order to separate the evil from the good,
וְיוּשְׁאַר לָרְשָׁעִים, וְהַטּוֹב יִרְשׁוּ צַדִּיקִים;
— leaving it to the wicked, while the righteous inherit the good;
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁכָּתַב הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה
— and as the Ari of blessed memory wrote
בְּמַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (חֲגִיגָה טו.):
— concerning what they said (Chagigah 15a):
"זָכָה צַדִּיק – נוֹטֵל חֶלְקוֹ וְחֵלֶק חֲבֵירוֹ בְּגַן עֵדֶן,
— "If the righteous merits, he takes his portion and his peer's portion in Gan Eden;
נִתְחַיֵּיב רָשָׁע – נוֹטֵל חֶלְקוֹ וְחֵלֶק חֲבֵירוֹ בְּגֵיהִנָּם".
— if the wicked is convicted, he takes his portion and his peer's portion in Gehenna."
דְּצַדִּיק, "וְעַמֵּךְ כֻּלָּם צַדִּיקִים",
— For the righteous—"and your people are all righteous"—
וְיֵשׁ לְעֻמָּתוֹ נֶפֶשׁ שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ נִיצוֹץ טוֹב מֵחֶלְקוֹ,
— and there exists opposite him a soul holding a good spark belonging to his share,
וּכְשֶׁזּוֹכֶה נוֹטֵל הוּא הַטּוֹב
— and when he merits, he takes the good,
וְהָרַע נִפְרָד לְהַנֶּפֶשׁ שֶׁלְּעֻמָּתוֹ בַּקְּלִיפָּה.
— and the evil is separated unto the soul opposite him within the kelipah.
וּבְדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל וְדוֹר הַפְלָגָה הָיָה מְעוֹרְבָב שָׁם נַפְשׁוֹת יִשְׂרָאֵל גַּם כֵּן,
— And in the Generation of the Flood and the Generation of the Dispersion, the souls of Israel were intermingled there as well,
שֶׁהֲרֵי מֵהֶן יָצְאוּ כָּל נְפָשׁוֹת הַגְּבוֹהוֹת וְהַקְּדוֹשׁוֹת;
— for from them emerged all the exalted and holy souls;
רַק כֵּיוָן שֶׁהָיָה מְעוֹרְבָב בֵּין ע' הַקְּלִיפּוֹת נִתְגַּבֵּר הָרַע.
— only because it was intermingled among the seventy kelipot, evil gained dominance.
וְכֵן כָּתַב הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה,
— And so wrote the Ari of blessed memory,
שֶׁנַּפְשׁוֹת דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל הָיוּ בְּמִצְרַיִם
— that the souls of the Generation of the Flood were reincarnated in Egypt
וְנִגְזַר עֲלֵיהֶם "כָּל הַבֵּן הַיִּלּוֹד הַיְאֹרָה תַּשְׁלִיכֻהוּ",
— and decreed upon them: "Every son that is born you shall cast into the river,"
וְנַפְשׁוֹת דּוֹר הַפְלָגָה הָיוּ גַּם כֵּן בְּמִצְרַיִם
— and the souls of the Generation of the Dispersion were likewise in Egypt
וְנִגְזַר עֲלֵיהֶם הָעֲבוֹדָה בְּחֹמֶר וּבִלְבֵנִים.
— and decreed upon them the labor in mortar and bricks.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ: כֵּיוָן שֶׁנִּסְתַּכֵּל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא בְּדוֹר הַמַּבּוּל וּבְדוֹר הַפְלָגָה וְכוּלֵי,
— And this is what they said: once the Holy One looked upon the Generation of the Flood and Dispersion, etc.,
וְאִם לֹא הָיָה נִגְנַז הָאוֹר,
— and had the light not been concealed,
הָיָה הַטּוֹב שֶׁבָּהֶן זוֹכֶה לֵהָנוֹת מֵאוֹר הָרִאשׁוֹן
— the good within them would have merited to enjoy the Primordial Light,
וְהָרַע יִתְגַּבֵּר בְּכָל פַּעַם כְּמוֹ בַּאֲכִילַת עֵץ הַחַיִּים,
— and the evil would intensify repeatedly just as with the eating of the tree of life;
דְּכֵיוָן שֶׁהָיָה הָעִרְבּוּב טוֹב וָרָע,
— for since there was a mixture of good and evil,
יוּכַל הַטּוֹב לִזְכּוֹת לָאוֹר
— the good could merit the light
וְהָרַע שֶׁבּוֹ יִתְגַּבֵּר וְיוּכְלוּ עוֹד לְהָרַע בְּכֹחַ זֶה;
— and the evil within it would strengthen and empower them to do further evil through that very power;
וְעַל כֵּן עָמַד וּגְנָזוֹ מֵהֶם,
— and therefore He arose and concealed it from them,
שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וַיִּמָּנַע מֵרְשָׁעִים אוֹרָם".
— as it is said: "And from the wicked their light is withheld."
וְזֶה גַּם כֵּן כַּוָּנַת הַזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ הַנִּזְכָּר לְעֵיל:
— And this is likewise the intention of the holy Zohar cited above:
"דְּלָא יֵהֲנוּן מִנֵּיהּ חַיָּיבֵי עָלְמָא".
— "So that the wicked of the world would not benefit from it."

paragraphs.text: Sefer HaBahir 160: “This teaches that before the world was created, it arose in thought to create a great light to illuminate. A great light was created which no creature could master. The Holy One, blessed be He, foresaw that they could not bear it. He took a seventh and placed it there for them, and stored away the rest for the righteous in the future. He said: “If they merit this seventh and guard it, I will give them this in the final world.” This is the World to Come, which had already come before the six days of Creation.”

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 11:2: ““God blessed the seventh day [and sanctified it]” – Rabbi Yishmael said: He blessed it with manna and He sanctified it with manna. He blessed it with manna in that all the days of the week one omer [of manna] would fall, while on the day before Shabbat two omers would fall. He sanctified it with manna, as it did not fall on it [on Shabbat] at all. Rabbi Natan says: He blessed it with manna and sanctified it with a blessing. Rabbi Yitzḥak said: He blessed it with manna and sanctified it through the gatherer. He blessed it with apparel. Rav Huna said: He should change his clothing. Rabbi Ḥiyya said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: He should mix [garments]. Avin bar Ḥisdai said: He should lower [his garments]. Rabbi Yirmeya and Rabbi Ze’eira were walking together [on Shabbat], and the outer garment of Rabbi Yirmeya was raised up, but Rabbi Ze’eira lowered his. This shows that one should lower [one’s garments for Shabbat]. Rabbi Elazar says: He blessed it with [the Shabbat] candle, and there was an incident involving me [that illustrates this]. One time I kindled a candle on Shabbat eve, and I came and found it burning at the conclusion of Shabbat, and nothing [of the oil] was diminished. He blessed it with the radiance of a person’s face, He sanctified it with the radiance of a person’s face. The radiance of a person’s face all the days of the week is not comparable to the way it is on Shabbat. He blessed it with the lights. Rabbi Shimon bar Yehuda of Kefar Akko says in the name of Rabbi Shimon: Even though the lights were cursed on the day before Shabbat, they were not stricken until the conclusion of Shabbat. This is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, and not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Ami, as Rabbi Ami said: Adam the first man, his glory did not spend the night with him. What is the source? “Man [adam] will not go to rest in his splendor; he is like the beasts that perish” (Psalms 49:13). The Rabbis say: His glory did spend the night with him, and only at the conclusion of Shabbat was his radiance taken from him, as He expelled him from the Garden of Eden. That is what is written: “You alter his countenance and send him away” (Job 14:20). When the sun set on Shabbat eve, the Holy One blessed be He sought to put away the [primordial] light, but He accorded honor to Shabbat. That is what is written: “God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it” – He blessed it with light. When the sun set on Shabbat eve the [primordial] light continued to function. Everyone began praising [God]; that is what is written: “Under all the heavens they sing His praises, and His light is to the ends of the earth” (Job 37:3). Why was this? Because “His light is to the ends of the earth.” Rabbi Yehuda bar Rabbi Simon said: By the light that the Holy One blessed be He created on the first day, a person could look out and see from one end of the world to the other end. When the Holy One blessed be He looked at the people of the generation of the Flood and the people of the generation of the Dispersion, whose actions were to be corrupt, He arose and hid it away and designated it for the righteous in the future. From where is it derived that He hid it away? It is as it is stated: “Their light will be withheld from the wicked, and the upraised arm will be broken” (Job 38:15). And from where is it derived that He designated it for the righteous in the future? It is as it is stated: “But the path of the righteous is like a dawning light, growing brighter until the day is established” (Proverbs 4:18). Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Ze’eira: That [primordial] light functioned for thirty-six hours – twelve on the day before Shabbat, twelve on the night of Shabbat, and twelve on Shabbat. As the sun set at the conclusion of Shabbat, darkness began approaching, and Adam the first man became afraid, as it is stated: “And I said that darkness will envelop me [yeshufeni]; night for me is light,” (Psalms 139:11) – that one [the serpent] in whose regard it is written: “He will strike your head [yeshufekha], and you will strike his heel [teshufenu]” (Genesis 3:15), is now coming to confront me. What did the Holy One blessed be He do? He prepared for him two flint stones and he struck them one against the other. Light emerged from them and he recited a blessing over it. That is what is written: “Night for me is light.” What blessing did he recite over it? [Blessed be God] Who creates the lights of fire. This is in accordance with the opinion of Shmuel, as Shmuel said: Why does one recite a blessing over light at the conclusion of Shabbat? It is because that time was the beginning of its creation. Rav Huna in the name of Rav and Rabbi Abahu in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One recites a blessing over it [light] at the conclusion of Yom Kippur, as well, because fire rested all that day.”

rich.text: Bereshit Rabbah 11:2

: ““God blessed the seventh day [and sanctified it]” – Rabbi Yishmael said: He blessed it with manna and He sanctified it with manna. He blessed it with manna in that all the days of the week one omer [of manna] would fall, while on the day before Shabbat two omers would fall. He sanctified it with manna, as it did not fall on it [on Shabbat] at all. Rabbi Natan says: He blessed it with manna and sanctified it with a blessing. Rabbi Yitzḥak said: He blessed it with manna and sanctified it through the gatherer. He blessed it with apparel. Rav Huna said: He should change his clothing. Rabbi Ḥiyya said in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan: He should mix [garments]. Avin bar Ḥisdai said: He should lower [his garments]. Rabbi Yirmeya and Rabbi Ze’eira were walking together [on Shabbat], and the outer garment of Rabbi Yirmeya was raised up, but Rabbi Ze’eira lowered his. This shows that one should lower [one’s garments for Shabbat]. Rabbi Elazar says: He blessed it with [the Shabbat] candle, and there was an incident involving me [that illustrates this]. One time I kindled a candle on Shabbat eve, and I came and found it burning at the conclusion of Shabbat, and nothing [of the oil] was diminished. He blessed it with the radiance of a person’s face, He sanctified it with the radiance of a person’s face. The radiance of a person’s face all the days of the week is not comparable to the way it is on Shabbat. He blessed it with the lights. Rabbi Shimon bar Yehuda of Kefar Akko says in the name of Rabbi Shimon: Even though the lights were cursed on the day before Shabbat, they were not stricken until the conclusion of Shabbat. This is in accordance with the opinion of the Rabbis, and not in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Ami, as Rabbi Ami said: Adam the first man, his glory did not spend the night with him. What is the source? “Man [adam] will not go to rest in his splendor; he is like the beasts that perish” (Psalms 49:13). The Rabbis say: His glory did spend the night with him, and only at the conclusion of Shabbat was his radiance taken from him, as He expelled him from the Garden of Eden. That is what is written: “You alter his countenance and send him away” (Job 14:20). When the sun set on Shabbat eve, the Holy One blessed be He sought to put away the [primordial] light, but He accorded honor to Shabbat. That is what is written: “God blessed the seventh day, and sanctified it” – He blessed it with light. When the sun set on Shabbat eve the [primordial] light continued to function. Everyone began praising [God]; that is what is written: “Under all the heavens they sing His praises, and His light is to the ends of the earth” (Job 37:3). Why was this? Because “His light is to the ends of the earth.” Rabbi Yehuda bar Rabbi Simon said: By the light that the Holy One blessed be He created on the first day, a person could look out and see from one end of the world to the other end. When the Holy One blessed be He looked at the people of the generation of the Flood and the people of the generation of the Dispersion, whose actions were to be corrupt, He arose and hid it away and designated it for the righteous in the future. From where is it derived that He hid it away? It is as it is stated: “Their light will be withheld from the wicked, and the upraised arm will be broken” (Job 38:15). And from where is it derived that He designated it for the righteous in the future? It is as it is stated: “But the path of the righteous is like a dawning light, growing brighter until the day is established” (Proverbs 4:18). Rabbi Levi said in the name of Rabbi Ze’eira: That [primordial] light functioned for thirty-six hours – twelve on the day before Shabbat, twelve on the night of Shabbat, and twelve on Shabbat. As the sun set at the conclusion of Shabbat, darkness began approaching, and Adam the first man became afraid, as it is stated: “And I said that darkness will envelop me [yeshufeni]; night for me is light,” (Psalms 139:11) – that one [the serpent] in whose regard it is written: “He will strike your head [yeshufekha], and you will strike his heel [teshufenu]” (Genesis 3:15), is now coming to confront me. What did the Holy One blessed be He do? He prepared for him two flint stones and he struck them one against the other. Light emerged from them and he recited a blessing over it. That is what is written: “Night for me is light.” What blessing did he recite over it? [Blessed be God] Who creates the lights of fire. This is in accordance with the opinion of Shmuel, as Shmuel said: Why does one recite a blessing over light at the conclusion of Shabbat? It is because that time was the beginning of its creation. Rav Huna in the name of Rav and Rabbi Abahu in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One recites a blessing over it [light] at the conclusion of Yom Kippur, as well, because fire rested all that day.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Beshalach 26:348: “Then HE (Moses) CRIED UNTO THE LORD, AND THE LORD SHOWED HIM A TREE, without deviating right or left. This is symbolized by the sound of the Shophar, which is thrust forth in a straight line from a narrow opening and breaks through the firmaments in order to stir up the Spirit above. It is true, we are told, that “Isaac did meditate in the field” (Gen. 24, 63); but there are special reasons for this; and besides, the field where he prayed was not an ordinary field. WHICH, WHEN HE CAST IT INTO THE WATERS, THE WATERS WERE MADE SWEET. The tree is a symbol of the Torah, which is “a tree of life to those who lay hold upon her” (Prov. 3, 18), and the Torah and the Holy One, blessed be He, are one.’ R. Abba said: ‘The “Tree” is a direct symbol of the Holy One, for it says: “The tree of the field is (the supernal) Adam” (Deut. 20, 19). The “field” is the “Field of the holy apples”. Thus, when the light of their King’s glory manifested itself to them, “the waters were made sweet”, and the accuser became an intercessor.’”

paragraphs.text: Chagigah 15a: ‘Aḥer said to him: Rabbi Akiva, your teacher, did not say so, but explained the verse as follows: Everything has its opposite: He created the righteous, He created the wicked; He created the Garden of Eden, He created Gehenna. Each and every person has two portions, one in the Garden of Eden and one in Gehenna. If he merits it, by becoming righteous, he takes his portion and the portion of his wicked colleague in the Garden of Eden; if he is found culpable by becoming wicked, he takes his portion and the portion of his colleague in Gehenna.’

paragraphs.text: Derekh Hashem, Part One, On Mankind 9: “Beyond all this, however, His blessed attribute of judgment decreed that neither man nor the world could henceforth attain perfection while still in their damaged form—the form they now possess, in which evil has increased. They must necessarily pass through a stage of dissolution: death for man, and dissolution for all the other beings that became damaged along with him. The soul cannot purify the body until it first leaves it and the body dies and decomposes. The body will then be built anew, and the soul will enter and purify it. Likewise, the entire world will lose its present form and be rebuilt in another form suited to perfection.”

h: Guarding Shabbat from Sin and the Light of Wisdom

p: וּבְשַׁבָּת דִּכְתִיב: "שֹׁמֵר שַׁבָּת מֵחַלְּלוֹ וְשֹׁמֵר יָדוֹ מֵעֲשׂוֹת כָּל רָע",
— And on Shabbat, concerning which it is written: "Guarding the Sabbath from profaning it, and keeping his hand from doing any evil";
וּבַמְּכִילְתָּא אִיתָא: שֶׁמְּשׁוּמָּר מִן הָעֲבֵירָה,
— and in the Mekhilta it is stated: that he is safeguarded from transgression;
וּבִפְרִי עֵץ חַיִּים אִיתָא הַלָּשׁוֹן: שֶׁנִּיצּוֹל מִקִּטְרוּג יֵצֶר הָרָע;
— and in Pri Etz Chayyim the wording is: that he is rescued from the accusation of the evil inclination;
וְהַיְינוּ עַל יְדֵי שְׁמִירַת שַׁבָּת תַּתָּאָה.
— and that is achieved through the observance of the lower Shabbat.
וּמִי שֶׁזּוֹכֶה עַל יְדֵי זֶה לְשַׁבָּת עִלָּאָה,
— And whoever merits through this the higher Shabbat,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בַּתִּיקּוּנִים (תִּיקּוּן מח):
— as written in the Tikkunim (Tikkun 48):
"תְּרֵין זִמְנִין אִדְכַּר הָכָא שַׁבָּת לָקֳבֵל שְׁכִינְתָּא עִלָּאָה וְתַתָּאָה,
— "Two times is Shabbat mentioned here corresponding to the supernal and lower Shechinah,
וְהַיְינוּ שַׁבָּת עִלָּאָה שַׁבָּת תַּתָּאָה לְדֹרֹתָם,
— namely supernal Shabbat and lower Shabbat throughout their generations;
זַכָּאָה מַאן דְּעָבֵיד לוֹן בְּשַׁבָּת דִּירָה בִּתְרֵי בָּתֵּי לִבָּא
— fortunate is he who makes for them on Shabbat a dwelling in the two chambers of the heart,
וְאִתְפַּנֵּי יֵצֶר הָרָע מִן תַּמָּן וְכוּלֵי",
— and the evil inclination is cleared away from there, etc.",
אָז יְכוֹלִים לְבַקֵּשׁ "נְהוֹרֵיהּ יִשְׁרֵי בָהּ",
— then they are able to request "May His light dwell within it,"
שֶׁיִּזְכֶּה לָאוֹר הַגָּנוּז הַמִּתְגַּלֶּה בְּשַׁבָּת.
— that he merit the concealed light that is revealed on Shabbat.
וּמְבַקְּשִׁים זֶה בִּסְעוּדָה שְׁנִיָּה סְעוֹדָתָא דְּעַתִּיקָא,
— And we request this during the second meal, the meal of Atika,
שֶׁחֲשָׁבָהּ הָאֲרִ״י זִכְרוֹנוֹ לִבְרָכָה נֶגֶד קְדוּשַׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— which the Ari of blessed memory reckoned corresponding to the holiness of our father Abraham, peace be upon him,
שֶׁבְּחִינַת קְדוּשָׁתוֹ הוּא הָאוֹר,
— whose dimension of holiness is the light,
כִּדְאִיתָא בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה (פָּרָשָׁה זוֹ):
— as brought in Midrash Rabbah (in this portion):
"וְחֹשֶׁךְ זֶה דּוֹרוֹ שֶׁל אֱנוֹשׁ,
— "'And darkness'—this is the Generation of Enosh;
עַל פְּנֵי תְהוֹם זֶה דּוֹר הַמַּבּוּל וְכוּלֵי;
— 'upon the face of the deep'—this is the Generation of the Flood, etc.;
אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: עַד מָתַי יְהֵא הָעוֹלָם מִתְנַהֵג בַּאֲפֵלָה,
— the Holy One, blessed be He, said: How long shall the world proceed in darkness?
תָּבוֹא הָאוֹרָה, יְהִי אוֹר – זֶה אַבְרָהָם",
— Let the light come: 'Let there be light'—this is Abraham,"
וְהוּא מַאֲמָר רִאשׁוֹן.
— and it is the first utterance.
אַף דִּבְרֵאשִׁית נַמֵּי מַאֲמָר הוּא,
— Even though 'In the beginning' is also an utterance,
הוּא נֶגֶד שֵׂכֶל הַנֶּעְלָם מִכָּל רַעְיוֹן,
— it corresponds to the intellect concealed from all contemplation,
וּמַאֲמַר "יְהִי אוֹר" מְרַמֵּז לִבְחִינַת חָכְמָה,
— and the utterance "Let there be light" alludes to the aspect of Chokhmah (Wisdom),
רֵאשִׁית הִתְגַּלּוּת יֵשׁ מֵאַיִן.
— the beginning of the manifest revelation of something out of nothing.
וְזֶה קְדוּשַׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— And this is the sanctity of our father Abraham, peace be upon him,
שֶׁהֵאִיר לָעוֹלָם בְּחָכְמָתוֹ לֵידַע הַשְׁגָּחָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ שְׁמוֹ,
— who illuminated the world with his wisdom to recognize the providence of Hashem, blessed be His Name,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר עָלָיו: "מִי הֵעִיר מִמִּזְרָח צֶדֶק", כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה.
— as it is said concerning him: "Who raised up righteousness from the east," as written in Midrash Rabbah.
עַד שֶׁנִּתְקַשֵּׁר בָּזֶה בְּסוֹף יָמָיו בִּבְחִינַת עַתִּיקָא,
— Until he bound himself in this at the end of his days to the dimension of Atika,
שֶׁהוּא אֱמוּנָה לְמַעְלָה מִן הַדַּעַת,
— which is faith transcending mortal intellect,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וְהֶאֱמִן בַּה'", עַל בְּשׂוֹרַת הַבָּנִים,
— as it is said: "And he believed in Hashem," regarding the glad tidings of children,
אַף שֶׁהָיָה רוֹאֶה בְּהַשָּׂגָתוֹ בְּחָכְמָה שֶׁאֵין אוֹפֶן שֶׁיִּהְיוּ לוֹ בָּנִים,
— even though he saw in his wisdom that there was no natural way for him to have children,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "כִּי אֶחָד קְרָאתִיו",
— as it is said: "For I called him one,"
שֶׁעַל פִּי תּוֹלְדָתוֹ הָיָה בִּבְחִינַת אֶחָד בְּלֹא בָּנִים;
— for according to his nature he was in the status of one without children;
אֲבָל עַל יְדֵי מַה שֶּׁנִּתְקַשֵּׁר בִּבְחִינַת עַתִּיקָא שֶׁהוּא מַזָּלָא
— yet through binding himself to the aspect of Atika which is Mazala (the supernal source),
כִּדְאִיתָא בַּזֹּהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ (חֵלֶק ג, עט עַמּוּד ב),
— as brought in the holy Zohar (Part III, 79b),
שֶׁהוּא הַשּׁוֹרֶשׁ לְמַעְלָה מֵהַשָּׂגַת הָאָדָם,
— which is the Root transcending human comprehension,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (מְגִילָּה ג.): "אַף עַל גַּב דְּאִינְהוּ לָא חֲזוֹ מַזְלַיְיהוּ חֲזֵי",
— as written in Megillah (3a): "Even though they did not see, their mazal saw,"
וְעַל יְדֵי כֹּחַ עַתִּיקָא שֶׁהוּא בְּחִינַת "אֵין מַזָּל לְיִשְׂרָאֵל" זָכָה לְבָנִים.
— and through the power of Atika, which is the realm of "Israel is not subject to planetary mazal," he merited children.
לָכֵן אָנוּ אוֹמְרִים בִּסְעוּדָתָא דְּעַתִּיקָא: "נְהוֹרֵיהּ יִשְׁרֵי בָהּ",
— Therefore we recite at the meal of Atika: "May His light dwell within it,"
שֶׁהוּא קְדוּשַׁת אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם.
— which is the sanctity of our father Abraham, peace be upon him.
"בְּחַמְרָא טָבָא",
— "With fine wine,"
שֶׁהוּא מְרוּמָּז עַל תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה שֶׁנִּמְשְׁלָה לְיַיִן,
— which alludes to the Oral Torah that is compared to wine,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: "וּשְׁתוּ בְּיַיִן מָסָכְתִּי" – יֵינָא דְּאוֹרַיְיתָא דִּבְעַל פֶּה,
— as it is said: "And drink of the wine that I have mingled"—the wine of the Oral Torah;
וְהוּא בְּחִינַת חָכְמָה שֶׁל אַבְרָהָם אָבִינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם,
— and this is the aspect of the wisdom of our father Abraham, peace be upon him,
כְּמַאֲמָרָם זִכְרוֹנָם לִבְרָכָה (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה פָּרָשָׁה סא):
— as our Sages of blessed memory stated (Bereishit Rabbah, Parashah 61):
"אָב לֹא לִמְּדוֹ וְרַב לֹא הָיָה לוֹ,
— "A father did not teach him and a master he did not have,
אֶלָּא זִמֵּן לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שְׁתֵּי כִלְיוֹתָיו כִּשְׁנֵי רַבָּנִים,
— rather the Holy One, blessed be He, made his two kidneys like two rabbis,
וְהָיוּ נוֹבְעוֹת וּמְלַמְּדִים אוֹתוֹ תּוֹרָה וְחָכְמָה".
— and they welled forth and taught him Torah and wisdom."

paragraphs.text: Tikkunei Zohar 85a:3: “Bereishis contains “two” and “Shabbos,” in this arrangement: beis–reishis, bara–shis. They are two Shabbosos, of which it says: “The children of Israel shall observe the Shabbos, to make the Shabbos.” Shabbos is mentioned here twice, corresponding to the upper and lower Shechinah. “For their generations”—what does this mean? Fortunate is the one who makes a dwelling for them on Shabbos in the two chambers of the heart, so that the evil inclination, which is the profanation of Shabbos, is removed from there.”

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Achrei Mot 72:405-75:413: ‘It is written, “The burnt offering of the Sabbath beside (‘al, lit. upon) the continual burnt offering” (Num. 28, 10). The word ‘al here signifies that the thought should be directed to the very highest more than on other days. Similarly it is written, “And Hannah prayed to (‘al, lit. upon) the Lord” (I Sam. 1, 19), because children depend upon the holy mazzal, as we have pointed out.’

paragraphs.text: Bereshit Rabbah 61:1: ““Abraham took another wife, and her name was Ketura” (Genesis 25:1). “Abraham took another wife, and her name was Ketura.” It is written: “Happy is the man who has not walked…” (Psalms 1:1). “Who has not walked in the counsel of the wicked” (Psalms 1:1) – this [“the wicked”] refers to the generation of the Dispersion. “Has not stood in the path of sinners” (Psalms 1:1) – these are the people of Sodom, as it is stated: “The people of Sodom were extremely wicked and sinful to the Lord” (Genesis 13:13). “And has not sat [yashav] in the company of the insolent one” (Psalms 1:1) – this refers to Avimelekh, as it is stated: “Behold my land is before you, [dwell [shev] wherever it suits you]…” (Genesis 20:15). “But whose desire is the Torah of the Lord” (Psalms 1:2) – “For I love him, so that he will command [his children and his household after him that they keep the way of the Lord]…” (Genesis 18:19). “And he meditates on His Torah” (Psalms 1:2) – Rabbi Shimon said: He [Abraham] had no father to teach him, and he did not have a teacher. From where, then, did he learn Torah? The answer is that the Holy One blessed be He set his two kidneys [kilyotav] as two teachers of a sort, and they would flow forth and teach him Torah and wisdom. That is what is written: “I bless the Lord who counsels me, even on nights when my thoughts [khilyotai] are anguished” (Psalms 16:7). “He will be like a tree planted” (Psalms 1:3) – the Holy One blessed be He planted him in the Land of Israel. “Which brings forth its fruit in season” (Psalms 1:3) – this refers to Ishmael. “And whose leaf does not wither” (Psalms 1:3) – this refers to Isaac. “And whatever he does will prosper” (Psalms 1:3) – this refers to the sons of Ketura, as it is stated: “Abraham took another wife, and her name was Ketura.””
